content: Lopinavir is metabolized by the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4, and its interactions with other drugs can lead to significant changes in drug levels and effects. Below are detailed descriptions of these interactions: 1. Siponimod and Lopinavir: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, which can lead to cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 2. Lopinavir and Sirolimus: Lopinavir increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Lopinavir and Solifenacin: Lopinavir increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Lopinavir and Sonidegib: Lopinavir increases sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 5. Lopinavir and Sorafenib: Lopinavir increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Lopinavir and Sparsentan: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergy. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 7. St. John’s Wort and Lopinavir: St. John’s Wort decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Lopinavir and Stiripentol: Lopinavir increases stiripentol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Lopinavir and Sunitinib: Lopinavir increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Lopinavir and Suvorexant: Lopinavir increases suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Lopinavir and Tacrolimus: Lopinavir increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Lopinavir and Tadalafil: Lopinavir increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing severe adverse effects such as hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Lopinavir and Tamoxifen: Lopinavir decreases tamoxifen metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Lopinavir and Tamsulosin: Lopinavir increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of toxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Lopinavir and Tazemetostat: Lopinavir increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Lopinavir and Temsirolimus: Lopinavir increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Lopinavir and Tetrabenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Lopinavir and Tiagabine: Lopinavir increases tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Tipranavir and Lopinavir: Tipranavir decreases lopinavir levels through an unspecified mechanism, while lopinavir increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Lopinavir and Tofacitinib: Lopinavir increases tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Lopinavir and Tolterodine: Lopinavir increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Lopinavir and Tolvaptan: Lopinavir increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Lopinavir and Topotecan: Lopinavir increases topotecan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Lopinavir and Trabectedin: Lopinavir increases trabectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If co-administration is necessary, administer the CYP3A4 inhibitor one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 25. Lopinavir and Trazodone: Lopinavir increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Lopinavir and Trimethoprim: Lopinavir increases trimethoprim levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Lopinavir and Triptorelin: Co-administration increases the risk of torsades de pointes due to QTc prolongation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Lopinavir and Tucatinib: Lopinavir increases tucatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as per product labeling. 29. Lopinavir and Ulipristal: Lopinavir increases ulipristal levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Lopinavir and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol: Co-administration increases the risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Lopinavir and Vandetanib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Lopinavir and Vemurafenib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Lopinavir and Verapamil: Lopinavir increases verapamil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Lopinavir and Vilazodone: Lopinavir increases vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 35. Lopinavir and Vinblastine: Lopinavir increases vinblastine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Lopinavir and Vincristine: Lopinavir increases vincristine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Lopinavir and Vorapaxar: Lopinavir increases vorapaxar levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Lopinavir and Voriconazole: Lopinavir increases voriconazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Lopinavir and Vorinostat: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Lopinavir and Vortioxetine: Lopinavir increases vortioxetine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Reduce the vortioxetine dose by 50%. 41. Lopinavir and Voxilaprevir: Lopinavir increases voxilaprevir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Lopinavir and Abemaciclib: Lopinavir increases abemaciclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required. 43. Lopinavir and Acarbose: Lopinavir decreases the effects of acarbose due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor for hyperglycemia. 44. Lopinavir and Albiglutide: Lopinavir may cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely. 45. Lopinavir and Alfuzosin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Lopinavir and Amlodipine: Lopinavir increases amlodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Lopinavir and Amobarbital: Amobarbital decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Lopinavir and Apalutamide: Lopinavir increases apalutamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dose as needed. 49. Lopinavir and Apixaban: Lopinavir increases apixaban levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Lopinavir and Aprepitant: Both drugs increase each other’s levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Lopinavir and Armodafinil: Armodafinil decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Lopinavir and Artemether: Lopinavir may increase or decrease artemether levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Lopinavir and Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Lopinavir and Azithromycin: Azithromycin increases lopinavir toxicity due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Lopinavir and Bedaquiline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor ECG closely. 56. Lopinavir and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Lopinavir increases hydrocodone levels, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 57. Lopinavir and Berotralstat: Lopinavir increases berotralstat levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Lopinavir and Betrixaban: Lopinavir increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Reduce the betrixaban dose accordingly. 59. Lopinavir and Bortezomib: Lopinavir increases bortezomib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Lopinavir and Bosentan: Bosentan decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Lopinavir and Brentuximab Vedotin: Lopinavir increases brentuximab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for adverse reactions. 62. Lopinavir and Brexpiprazole: Lopinavir increases brexpiprazole levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Reduce the brexpiprazole dose accordingly. 63. Lopinavir and Budesonide: Lopinavir increases budesonide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of Cushing’s syndrome or adrenal suppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Lopinavir and Buprenorphine: Lopinavir increases buprenorphine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for signs of toxicity and adjust the dose as needed. 65. Lopinavir and Butabarbital: Butabarbital decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Lopinavir and Calcifediol: Lopinavir may alter vitamin D metabolism, requiring dose adjustment of calcifediol. Monitor serum vitamin D, PTH, and calcium levels. 67. Lopinavir and Cannabidiol: Lopinavir increases cannabidiol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose. 68. Lopinavir and Capmatinib: Lopinavir increases capmatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Lopinavir and Cariprazine: Lopinavir increases cariprazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the cariprazine dose as needed. 70. Lopinavir and Cenobamate: Cenobamate decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Adjust the dose of lopinavir as needed. 71. Lopinavir and Ceritinib: Lopinavir increases ceritinib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Lopinavir and Chlordiazepoxide: Lopinavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider alternative benzodiazepines or reduce the dose. 73. Lopinavir and Chloroquine: Chloroquine increases lopinavir toxicity due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Lopinavir and Cholic Acid: Lopinavir decreases cholic acid elimination, potentially exacerbating bile salt accumulation. Monitor liver function tests. 75. Lopinavir and Ciclesonide: Lopinavir increases ciclesonide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of Cushing’s syndrome or adrenal suppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 76. Lopinavir and Citalopram: Lopinavir increases citalopram levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. Monitor ECG closely. 77. Lopinavir and Clonazepam: Lopinavir increases clonazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider alternative benzodiazepines or reduce the dose. 78. Lopinavir and Codeine: Lopinavir prevents the conversion of codeine to morphine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Lopinavir and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Lopinavir and Conjugated Estrogens: Lopinavir increases conjugated estrogen levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Lopinavir and Cortisone: Cortisone decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Lopinavir and Crizotinib: Lopinavir increases crizotinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration and monitor ECG closely. 83. Lopinavir and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 84. Lopinavir and Cyclophosphamide: Lopinavir increases cyclophosphamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 85. Lopinavir and Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 86. Lopinavir and Dabigatran: Lopinavir increases dabigatran levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid co-administration in patients with renal impairment. 87. Lopinavir and Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Adjust the lopinavir dose as needed. 88. Lopinavir and Darifenacin: Darifenacin increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 89. Lopinavir and Darolutamide: Lopinavir increases darolutamide levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dose as needed. 90. Lopinavir and Darunavir: Darunavir increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 91. Lopinavir and Dasatinib: Dasatinib increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 92. Lopinavir and Deferasirox: Deferasirox decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 93. Lopinavir and Deflazacort: Lopinavir increases deflazacort levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose. 94. Lopinavir and Desvenlafaxine: Lopinavir increases desvenlafaxine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for signs of toxicity. 95. Lopinavir and Deutetrabenazine: Lopinavir increases deutetrabenazine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Reduce the deutetrabenazine dose and monitor for QTc prolongation. 96. Lopinavir and Dexamethasone: Dexamethasone decreases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction, while lopinavir increases dexamethasone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 97. Lopinavir and DHEA (herbal): DHEA increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 98. Lopinavir and Diazepam: Lopinavir increases diazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider alternative benzodiazepines or reduce the dose. 99. Lopinavir and Diazoxide: Lopinavir may cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. 100. Lopinavir and Didanosine: Lopinavir increases gastric pH, reducing didanosine absorption. Administer didanosine one hour before or two hours after lopinavir. 101. Lopinavir and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Lopinavir alters estrogen and progestin levels. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular bleeding, and headache. 102. Lopinavir and Diltiazem: Diltiazem increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 103. Lopinavir and Docetaxel: Lopinavir increases docetaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 104. Lopinavir and Dofetilide: Lopinavir increases dofetilide levels, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and arrhythmias. Avoid or use alternatives. 105. Lopinavir and Doravirine: Lopinavir increases doravirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for toxicity and adjust the dose as needed.
